column2: req_desc

Health endpoint.
`GET /api/health` answers 200 on the published port once the app can reach PostgreSQL.

Public pages in the first HTML.
Every public page sends its headings and copy in the first HTML response, and the home page has exactly one level-one heading.

Not-found page.
Any address that is not a page answers 404 with the public chrome, "Page not found", "We could not find that page." and a "Back to home" link.

Privacy page.
`/privacy` states what an account, an enquiry and an invitation store, who reads them, and that the only cookie keeps a person signed in.

Accessible pages.
Every public page, sign in, sign up and the studio pages pass a WCAG 2.2 AA audit, and every generated picture carries alternative text.

Keyboard and focus.
Every control reached by keyboard shows a visible focus ring, and dialogs trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the control that opened them.

Phone layout.
At phone width no page scrolls sideways, the public header and the studio sidebar open as Menu drawers, the enquiry panel sits above the form, the composer spans the width and cards flow into one or two columns.

Reduced motion.
With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` no endless animation runs on the home page, the pricing page or a studio project with a rendering generation.

Self-contained pages.
Pages call no outside network service, show no cookie banner or upload control, and set at most one cookie, the session.

Nothing beyond scope.
No checkout, plan change, top-up, password reset, social sign in, upload, comment or account deletion address answers success, and none changes a balance.

Public site motion.
The home hero settles from slightly enlarged, the partner strip glides in an endless steady loop of about half a minute with faded edges, header menus fade in, and pricing prices cross-fade when the billing switch flips.

Studio motion.
Dialogs open with a soft zoom over a dimmed page, toasts rise and leave on their own, cards lift when pointed at, the phone drawer slides in from the left, and a saving Generate is unavailable with a turning spinner.

Generation motion.
A rendering card's bar fills while its placeholder breathes under a light sweep, a new card lands with a springy overshoot, and the finished picture fades in.

Light palette.
Grounds, ink, the single blue-violet accent, the soft highlights, the red errors, the green success note, the band gradient and the near-black footer follow Visual design.

Type and figures.
One neutral grotesk sans sets headlines and text, and credit balances, costs and history amounts sit in a monospace with aligned digits.

Components and icons.
Buttons wear the three skins, the named pills are fully round, cards float on a faint shadow, the composer is generously rounded, and icons are thin line drawings in the text colour.

Editorial lobby and tidy desk.
The public site breathes with rounded drawn frames under a frosted header, the studio is a slim sidebar beside a compact work area with the composer in the middle, and drawn pictures share one soft abstract language.

Rules held by the server.
Charges, refunds and idempotency are held by the database, email leaves over SMTP, roles and workspaces come from the token, and the server moves generations to Ready.

Global chrome.
The announcement band, the sticky header with its four menus and three buttons, and the footer carry the links and behaviour in Public site.

Public page controls.
The home tabs, the product tool tabs, the team plan questions, the licensing call to action and the research and resource cards behave as described in Public site.

Pricing controls.
`/pricing` opens on Individual and Yearly, the billing switch swaps yearly and monthly prices, the plan family tabs swap the cards, and each plan button leads where Public site says.

Plan and model catalogue.
`GET /api/plans` and `GET /api/models` return the six plans and three models with their whole-number prices, credits and limits.

Prompt library.
`/examples` and `GET /api/examples` narrow the eight examples by category and search, copy a prompt, and carry it into the studio through sign in.

Sign up.
Signing up creates an owner with a Free workspace, 125 recorded plan credits and "My first project", refuses a taken email in any case and invalid fields, and sends no email.

Sign in and sign out.
Seeded accounts sign in case-insensitively, wrong credentials get one message, studio pages need a session, and logging out ends the token.

Hashed passwords.
No users row holds a password in plain text.

Seed data.
The three accounts, two workspaces, three projects, three Ready generations and their credit histories are seeded once and send no email.

Studio needs a token.
Every studio endpoint answers 401 to a missing or malformed token, whatever the body claims, and changes nothing.

Workspaces kept apart.
Another workspace's projects, generations and outputs answer 404 and stay unchanged.

Projects.
Projects are created, listed newest first and renamed with names unique in any letter case, within the plan's project limit, from the New project dialog or the API.

Composer.
The studio home composer offers its named choices and defaults, follows every choice with its cost line, fills starter prompts from templates and lists the five newest generations.

Start and charge.
Starting a generation charges the server-computed cost once, lowers the shared balance at once and refuses invalid fields with 422.

Refused starts.
A start the balance cannot cover answers 402 and one beyond the parallel limit answers 409, each changing nothing.

Charged exactly once.
Repeats with one idempotency key, simultaneous same-key starts, simultaneous over-balance starts and a double click each leave one generation and one charge.

Rendering and output.
A generation is Ready 8 to 30 seconds after its start with no browser open, and its output is a deterministic SVG drawn from the prompt at its aspect, unavailable before Ready and to other workspaces.

Looping video and still image.
A Ready video's picture loops over its stated length and a Ready image's picture holds still.

Generation cards and cancel.
Generation cards show their details and update without a reload, and Cancel shows "Cancelled. <n> credits returned."

Refund once.
Cancelling a Queued or Rendering generation refunds its full cost exactly once, even under simultaneous cancels, and cancelling a Ready or cancelled one answers 409.

Credit history.
The balance always equals the sum of its entries with running balances never below zero, and `/studio/credits` shows the balance, the plan line and signed rows newest first.

Team page.
`/studio/team` shows seats, members and pending invitations, gives the Team owner Invite teammate and Revoke, hides them from members, and tells other plans that teams come from sales.

Invitation email.
Inviting sends exactly one email with the exact subject and the full join link, and refuses taken addresses and a tenth seat without sending.

Joining a team.
Accepting an invitation creates a Member, adds one 6,900 credit seat to the shared balance once, shows the full-page welcome, and leaves the link invalid.

Revoke and remove.
Revoked links stop working, removed members lose their session and sign in, nothing is refunded, and the owner cannot remove themselves.

Owner-only team management.
Members and owners of workspaces not on the Team plan are denied inviting, revoking and removing with 403, and nothing changes.

Enquiry form.
The enterprise and licensing forms show their fields and options, mark every failing field with an announced message, keep typed values and finish on a full-page confirmation.

Enquiry emails.
A valid enquiry is stored and sends exactly one sales email and one acknowledgement, a licensing enquiry is stored with its source, and an invalid one stores and sends nothing.

Stored change survives mail failure.
With mail undeliverable an invitation and an enquiry are still stored and answer success.
`/app/run.json` holds non-empty `install`, `build` and `serve` commands, and no `Dockerfile`, `start.sh` or compose file sits at the root of `/app`.
`/app/USER_README.md` lists the three seeded accounts with the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
The reserved `.browser_screenshots/` and `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root, empty.

`/app/package.json` names the stated libraries and builds with Vite, brings no second database, cache, queue, object store, identity, payment or mail provider, and its runtime `dependencies` are only the named libraries and their direct dependencies.
The app logs to standard output one line per HTTP request naming its method and path.
